chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of our companions, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The chicken is in the house and there is no rooster with her; she feeds on the sweepings and other things, and she lays an egg without the rooster mating with her. So what do you say about eating that egg?' He said to me: 'The egg, when it is from that whose flesh is eaten, there is no problem with it and with eating it, and it is permissible.'
ai.seo_question: Are eggs from hens without a rooster halal in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the permissibility of parthenogenetic eggs by linking their status to the general halal nature of the hen, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that the offspring inherits the ruling of the parent unless specific impurities are present. This hadith from al-Kafi provides a foundational textual basis for distinguishing between fertilized and unfertilized eggs in Islamic dietary law, emphasizing that the absence of a rooster does not render the egg impure or forbidden.
